title: AI Arms Race Puts Sovereign Supply Chains in the Spotlight
gist: Tobias Mann argues that for countries like South Korea, having a domestically sourced AI accelerator matters more than having the fastest one, because US export policy is unreliable. That makes Korean chipmakers FuriosaAI (which just raised a $620M Series D and is building a 2nm HBM4 chip with Broadcom) and Rebellions attractive to buyers in Asia-Pacific and EMEA who want non-American supply chains, even though their chips trail Nvidia's.

insights.claim: In the AI arms race, a domestically sourced or manufactured accelerator matters more to nations like South Korea than having the most powerful one, because it removes dependence on a US government that can withdraw access with little warning.
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann
insights.so_what: Sovereign AI policy creates protected demand for local accelerators regardless of how they compare with Nvidia.
